attacks.claim: The plan moves all customer documents, chunks, and embeddings to Nimbus Vector Store, which is currently provisioned only in us-east-2 (US). This violates the agreed DPA constraint that all customer-derived data be processed and stored in the EU, and the plan has no mitigation for this.
attacks.evidence: "Vector Store is in public preview and currently provisioned in us-east-2, with EU regions on Nimbus's GA roadmap."

attacks.claim: Retrieval of document chunks and embeddings into a non-EU region, plus cutover of all tenants in week 4, would breach customer DPAs; the plan does not gate cutover on EU residency being available.
attacks.evidence: "Week 4: cut all tenants over to Nimbus (generation + retrieval)."

attacks.claim: The regression eval suite is the agreed release gate for any model change, but the plan defers it to week 6+ after cutover. The 25-question blind comparison is not a substitute and cannot establish quality parity for a 70B-to-Atlas-L change plus removal of LoRA adapters.
attacks.evidence: "so the full regression suite run moves to post-migration hardening (week 6+) rather than blocking cutover."

attacks.claim: A sample of 25 support-inbox questions with two raters is far too small and unrepresentative to claim quality parity or better across practice areas; 19/25 preference has a wide confidence interval and no per-practice breakdown.
attacks.evidence: "Atlas-L was preferred in 19 of 25 and tied in 3. This confirms quality parity or better"

attacks.claim: Practice-area behaviour currently encoded in LoRA adapters is to be replaced by system prompts drafted in week 1 with no prototype or eval showing equivalence; the assumption that prompts reproduce fine-tuned behaviour is unprototyped.
attacks.evidence: "practice-area behaviour that lived in LoRA adapters moves into per-practice system prompts (drafted in week 1 by the applied team)."

attacks.claim: Week 3 irreversibly deletes fine-tuned checkpoints and LoRA adapters and releases the A100 reservation before cutover (week 4) and before any regression validation. If Nimbus quality or residency fails, there is no rollback to the model artifacts or GPU capacity.
attacks.evidence: "release the A100 reservation ... and delete fine-tuned checkpoints and LoRA adapters from object storage"

attacks.claim: Week 5 removes pgvector, vLLM manifests and the GPU node pool from Terraform, and the dual-write only covers new documents from week 2; rollback after week 5 requires rebuilding the entire retrieval stack and index.
attacks.evidence: "Week 5: remove pgvector, vLLM manifests, and GPU node pool from Terraform."

attacks.claim: Dual-write of new documents during week 2 has no described consistency, backfill-reconciliation, or failure handling between pgvector and Nimbus, so the two stores can silently diverge before cutover.
attacks.evidence: "re-embed corpus (~41M chunks) into Nimbus Vector Store; dual-write new documents."

attacks.claim: No timeouts, retry, fallback, or alerting are specified for a new external dependency that now sits on the critical path for every query; the on-call burden is not addressed.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: timeout/retry/fallback/alerting plan for Nimbus Inference API and Vector Store

attacks.claim: Peak ~40 req/s against a 120 req/s contracted tier leaves only 3x headroom with no quota-growth plan, and the plan does not account for the 10-100x load case or per-tenant rate isolation.
attacks.evidence: "our peak is ~40 req/s; our contracted tier allows 120 req/s."

attacks.claim: Re-embedding ~41M chunks in one week has no throughput estimate or rate-limit budgeting against the embedding API quota.
attacks.evidence: "Week 2: re-embed corpus (~41M chunks)"

attacks.claim: The savings math is unverified: the Nimbus generation line is an estimate with no token-volume basis, and the plan omits egress, one-time re-embedding cost, dual-running cost during weeks 2-4, and the 200k-context cost implications of the new long-context usage.
attacks.evidence: "Nimbus generation (est.) | $0 | $7,900"

attacks.claim: Storage line saving is stated as 6.2 TB but the table shows only $140/mo object storage for weights, which does not reconcile with a 6.2 TB storage line.
attacks.evidence: "to close out the 6.2 TB storage line" vs "Object storage (weights) | $140"

attacks.claim: Full replacement of self-hosted Llama-3.1-70B and LoRA adapters with a single proprietary provider for generation, embeddings, and vector storage creates single-vendor lock-in with no exit path or data export plan for 41M chunks and embeddings.
attacks.evidence: "Move generation + retrieval to Nimbus AI"; ABSENT: exit strategy or export path for embeddings and fine-tuned weights

attacks.claim: Zero data retention is cited but the plan does not verify it covers the Vector Store, embed-3 calls from ingest workers, or logs; retention of prompts and embeddings with a third party is not confirmed under the DPA.
attacks.evidence: "Zero data retention is enabled on our org account (signed addendum, ref NMB-ZDR-2291)."

attacks.claim: Per-tenant isolation depends on a tenant-scoped API key in a managed store; the plan does not describe how key scope is verified or tested, and key rotation of 30 days is not coordinated with the 41M-chunk store.
attacks.evidence: "Tenant isolation in Vector Store uses one collection per tenant with a tenant-scoped API key"

attacks.claim: Latency comparison is one measurement set from one week and shows improvement only from Frankfurt pods, which the plan has not reconciled with the Dublin generation region.
attacks.evidence: "Atlas-L p95 time-to-first-token measured at 640 ms from our Frankfurt pods ... Dublin (eu-west-1)"

attacks.claim: Dropping pgvector while Vector Store is in preview couples core retrieval to a preview API with no tested fallback.
attacks.evidence: "Vector Store is in public preview"

attacks.claim: The plan has no go/no-go criteria for cutover (residency, eval pass rate, latency, error rate) and no defined rollback trigger, so the cutover in week 4 is not gated on any measurable condition.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: cutover acceptance criteria and rollback triggers

attacks.claim: The agreed DPA constraint requires all customer documents and derived data (chunks, embeddings, prompts) to be processed and stored in the EU, yet the plan places Vector Store, which holds embeddings and chunks, in us-east-2, and the EU region is only on a roadmap. This violates the DPA before cutover.
attacks.evidence: "Vector Store is in public preview and currently provisioned in us-east-2, with EU regions on Nimbus's GA roadmap."

attacks.claim: Week 2 re-embeds the full 41M-chunk corpus and dual-writes new documents into the non-EU Vector Store, so customer-derived data would be stored outside the EU starting in week 2, not merely at cutover.
attacks.evidence: "Week 2: re-embed corpus (~41M chunks) into Nimbus Vector Store; dual-write new documents."

attacks.claim: The quality gate is bypassed. The 4,100-case regression suite is the agreed release gate for any model change, but the plan defers it to week 6+ after cutover. A 25-question blind comparison cannot establish parity, and the plan's own sample is too small and unrepresentative to support the claim.
attacks.evidence: "the full regression suite run moves to post-migration hardening (week 6+) rather than blocking cutover"

attacks.claim: Week 3 irreversibly destroys the rollback path (A100 reservation released, fine-tuned checkpoints and LoRA adapters deleted) before the week-4 cutover and before any regression evidence exists. If Atlas-L fails the eval or the vector store move fails, there is no way back to the current stack.
attacks.evidence: "release the A100 reservation ... and delete fine-tuned checkpoints and LoRA adapters from object storage"

attacks.claim: Week 5 removes pgvector and its index jobs from Terraform, so the retrieval fallback is also destroyed before the new retrieval path has been validated under production load.
attacks.evidence: "Week 5: remove pgvector, vLLM manifests, and GPU node pool from Terraform."

attacks.claim: Practice-area behaviour currently encoded in LoRA adapters is replaced by prompts drafted in week 1 by the applied team, with no validation step; behaviour drift across practice areas is unmeasured and only checked post-cutover.
attacks.evidence: "practice-area behaviour that lived in LoRA adapters moves into per-practice system prompts (drafted in week 1 by the applied team)."

attacks.claim: The latency claim is misleading. The 640 ms vs 910 ms comparison is measured from Frankfurt, but Nimbus generation is in Dublin, and the measurement does not state whether it includes retrieval, which will now cross to a us-east-2 store. The end-to-end latency impact is unknown.
attacks.evidence: "Atlas-L p95 time-to-first-token measured at 640 ms from our Frankfurt pods (1,000 requests, week of 10-05), vs 910 ms on vLLM."

attacks.claim: The 35% utilization and savings claims are stated without the underlying figures, and the cost table omits the cost of the US-hosted vector store's cross-region transfer and the migration itself. The $9,550 target is an estimate with no evidence attached.
attacks.evidence: "Nimbus generation (est.) | $0 | $7,900"

attacks.claim: The rate-limit headroom is thin. Peak is ~40 req/s against a 120 req/s tier, which leaves a 3x margin, but the plan has no burst or per-tenant quota analysis and dual-write during backfill adds load on top of peak.
attacks.evidence: "our peak is ~40 req/s; our contracted tier allows 120 req/s."

attacks.claim: Full dependence on a single vendor (generation, embeddings, and vector store), with pgvector and the self-hosted model removed in week 5, gives no practical exit path and no self-host fallback, and the custom fine-tuned weights are deleted in week 3.
attacks.evidence: "delete fine-tuned checkpoints and LoRA adapters from object storage"

attacks.claim: Per-tenant isolation relies on a tenant-scoped API key in a preview product, with no described isolation testing or audit logging for cross-tenant access.
attacks.evidence: "Tenant isolation in Vector Store uses one collection per tenant with a tenant-scoped API key"

attacks.claim: Zero data retention is claimed via a signed addendum, but the plan doesn't state whether ZDR also covers the Vector Store and embedding endpoints, or whether it covers the dual-write period.
attacks.evidence: "Zero data retention is enabled on our org account (signed addendum, ref NMB-ZDR-2291)."

attacks.claim: No rollback or failover plan is described for a Nimbus outage, and the on-call burden of the new vendor dependency is not assessed.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: failover path, Nimbus outage runbook, or alerting for vendor errors.

attacks.claim: Migration of 6.2 TB is cited as a storage saving, but the plan has no estimate of the time to re-embed 41M chunks, so the week-2 schedule is unverified.
attacks.evidence: "re-embed corpus (~41M chunks)"

attacks.claim: The plan's model is labelled Atlas-L with a 200k context window, but the 32k ceiling change is not tied to any evaluation of long-context answer quality, so the stated benefit is unverified.
attacks.evidence: "Nimbus Atlas-L supports 200k context natively; our current ceiling is 32k."

attacks.claim: The stated constraint is that all customer documents and derived data (chunks, embeddings, prompts) must be processed and stored in the EU. Vector Store is currently provisioned in us-east-2 and EU regions are only on a roadmap, yet the plan moves retrieval (which stores embeddings/chunks per tenant) there at Week 2 and cuts over at Week 4. This directly violates DPA terms.
attacks.evidence: "Vector Store is in public preview and currently provisioned in us-east-2, with EU regions on Nimbus's GA roadmap."

attacks.claim: The plan is internally contradictory on data residency: generation is claimed to be eu-west-1 but retrieval and embeddings are not pinned to any EU region, and the re-embed of ~41M chunks in Week 2 would push customer-derived data to the US-hosted store.
attacks.evidence: "Nimbus Vector Store (managed)... currently provisioned in us-east-2" alongside "re-embed corpus (~41M chunks) into Nimbus Vector Store"

attacks.claim: Quality parity is asserted from 25 blind-compared questions, but the 4,100-case regression suite is the agreed release gate for any model change and is deferred to week 6+ after cutover. The cutover therefore ships without the mandated gate.
attacks.evidence: "the full regression suite run moves to post-migration hardening (week 6+) rather than blocking cutover."

attacks.claim: Week 3 releases the A100 reservation and deletes fine-tuned checkpoints and LoRA adapters before the Week 4 cutover and before the regression suite has validated Nimbus. This removes the rollback path; if quality or residency fails, the old stack cannot be restored.
attacks.evidence: "release the A100 reservation... and delete fine-tuned checkpoints and LoRA adapters from object storage" (Week 3) vs "cut all tenants over to Nimbus" (Week 4) and "regression suite run" (Week 6+)

attacks.claim: Zero data retention is enabled only for generation on the org account; the plan does not state ZDR or retention terms for embed-3 or the Vector Store, nor does it address DPA sub-processor disclosure for a new US-based provider.
attacks.evidence: "Zero data retention is enabled on our org account (signed addendum, ref NMB-ZDR-2291)." (no equivalent for embeddings/store)

attacks.claim: Peak load of ~40 req/s against a 120 req/s contracted tier leaves only 3x headroom, and the plan does not address 10-100x growth or per-tenant quota fairness in the shared rate limit.
attacks.evidence: "our peak is ~40 req/s; our contracted tier allows 120 req/s."

attacks.claim: The latency claim is measured from Frankfurt pods against a Dublin endpoint for only one week of data, and the 640 ms vs 910 ms comparison is not stated to be on equivalent context lengths, so the improvement is not established.
attacks.evidence: "Atlas-L p95 time-to-first-token measured at 640 ms from our Frankfurt pods (1,000 requests, week of 10-05), vs 910 ms on vLLM."

attacks.claim: The cost table omits Vector Store/embedding variability and pgvector/infra savings are not netted, and generation cost is an estimate with no token-volume basis; the $9,550 figure is not evidenced.
attacks.evidence: "Nimbus generation (est.)   | $0        | $7,900"

attacks.claim: Cutover depends on a public-preview managed store with no stated SLA, fallback, or rollback to pgvector, and pgvector is removed in Week 5 before the cutover is proven stable.
attacks.evidence: "Week 5: remove pgvector, vLLM manifests, and GPU node pool from Terraform."

attacks.claim: Tenant isolation relies on per-tenant API keys in a preview product; no audit or penetration test of cross-tenant isolation is planned before cutover for confidential law-firm data.
attacks.evidence: "Tenant isolation in Vector Store uses one collection per tenant with a tenant-scoped API key"

attacks.claim: Full cutover to a single managed provider for generation, embeddings and retrieval creates lock-in with no stated exit path; the self-hosted Llama and LoRA weights are deleted in Week 3, eliminating the ability to revert or self-host.
attacks.evidence: "delete fine-tuned checkpoints and LoRA adapters from object storage"

attacks.claim: Replacing LoRA adapters with per-practice system prompts changes behaviour with no defined test that the prompts reproduce adapter behaviour, and the prompts are drafted in week 1 without eval gating.
attacks.evidence: "practice-area behaviour that lived in LoRA adapters moves into per-practice system prompts (drafted in week 1 by the applied team)."

attacks.claim: Prompts and retrieved chunks containing customer legal documents are sent to a third-party API; the plan does not describe the data-processing terms beyond ZDR on generation.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: DPA/sub-processor update covering Nimbus embeddings, vector store and prompt logging

attacks.claim: The 25-question sample is drawn from the support inbox, which may not represent the hard cases (long documents, multi-document reasoning) that the 200k context claim targets.
attacks.evidence: "ran 25 representative questions from the support inbox"
